claims.text: Thermally activated segregation of Cu to nanoparticle surfaces and grain boundaries governs the onset and progression of the FeNiCrCoCu phase transition.
Cu enrichment at surfaces and grain boundaries lowers the local melting temperature.
Cu enrichment nucleates a liquid-like surface layer.
The liquid-like layer propagates inward as temperature increases.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and compositionally homogeneous, with an approximately uniform elemental distribution.
Pre-annealing can be used to promote Cu surface enrichment relative to processing that maintains compositional homogeneity.
The comparison should use a slow, controlled temperature ramp near but below the bulk melting point in an inert atmosphere or high vacuum.
Preferential Cu diffusion produces a Cu-enriched surface and grain-boundary layer.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other constituents of FeNiCrCoCu.
Upon heating, Cu diffuses to energetically favorable surfaces and grain boundaries.
The Cu-rich liquid-like layer acts as a nucleation site for continued melting.
Cu-surface-enriched nanoparticles will show liquid-like behavior at significantly lower temperatures than uniformly mixed nanoparticles.
Melting in Cu-enriched nanoparticles will begin at the surface and progress gradually toward the core.
Nanoparticles with minimal segregation will undergo a more abrupt transition than Cu-enriched nanoparticles.
Uniformly mixed FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will remain solid until they reach the bulk melting temperature.
Impurities or reactive atmospheres could alter segregation dynamics and melting behavior.
The onset temperature, surface Cu enrichment, and surface-to-core melting-front rate can be measured using in situ TEM and EDS during a controlled thermal ramp.
If initially segregation-enhanced and uniform nanoparticles exhibit the same melting onset and similar surface compositions during heating, the proposed Cu-segregation mechanism is falsified.
